::: {#rem-racket-equivalence}
#### Checking an equivalence in Racket

A truth table is a loop over every combination of truth values,
so a program can check an equivalence.
In Racket, `for*/and` runs its body for every combination of `p` and `q`,
and returns `#f` as soon as the body returns `#f`, and `#t` if it never does:

```{racket}
#| code-fold: false
(for*/and ([p '(#t #f)]
           [q '(#t #f)])
  (equal? (or p (and p q)) p))
```

The result agrees with @exr-absorption.
With a new body, the same loop checks whether the two statements of @exr-not-and are equivalent:

```{racket}
#| code-fold: false
(for*/and ([p '(#t #f)]
           [q '(#t #f)])
  (equal? (not (and p q)) (and (not p) (not q))))
```

This result agrees with @exr-not-and.

:::
